source_text: Si enim pugnat medicina cum vulnere et mors peccato dicitur accidisse, ablationem mortis amotio peccati debet operari.
pass_a_gloss: For if medicine fights with the wound and death is said to have happened to sin, the removal of sin ought to work the taking-away of death.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5
LS vulnus; Blaise sin as wound
LS medicina; Blaise grace as medicine

pass_b_english: For if the medicine combats the wound, and death is said to have arisen through sin, removing sin should accomplish the removal of death.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian: Paul says death passed to all, not sin; distinguish temporal death from eternal punishment.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
